questions.prompt: Describe the net of a triangular prism.
solution_steps: Imagine unfolding a triangular prism flat, so every one of its faces lies in the same plane with none overlapping - this flattened-out shape is called its net.
A triangular prism's net is made up of: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.
So the answer is: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

questions.prompt: Angle GAK = 45°. Describe, step by step, how to construct the bisector of angle GAK using only a ruler and a pair of compasses.
solution_steps: Open the compasses to any radius and place the point on A (the vertex of the angle).
Draw an arc that crosses both arms of the angle, at a point on AG and a point on AK.
Without changing the compass radius, place the point on each of these two crossing points in turn and draw two more arcs so that they intersect each other.
Draw a straight line from A through the point where the two arcs intersect. This line is the bisector of angle GAK.
questions.final_answer: The straight line from A through the intersection of the two equal-radius arcs bisects angle GAK into two equal angles.
